newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Nov 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Nov 29.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The extra-judicial killings by the police of six drug suspects has cast Thailand back into the Dark Age and those responsible must be prosecuted, activist groups say. The killings in Suphan Buri province on Wednesday was condemned by the groups, which said the suspected amphetamine traffickers had surrendered and were handcuffed when they were shot. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- The Chavalit Yongchaiyudh Cabinet is to be presented to His Majesty the King today for approval and announced soon afterwards. Visanu Kreua-ngam, the cabinet secretary-general, says he is making final checks on their qualifications before going to the palace today. (BANGKOK POST)

- Two potential disasters in the city have been averted when a pair of buildings under construction were found to have incorrectable structural defects, with one building now slated for demolition and the process already under way with the other. (THE NATION) (BANGKOK POST)

- The central Bank has projected that exports could well show no growth this year after announcing that exports for the first nine months rose only 0.9 percent. It expresses concerns on the current account deficit and says the deficit would rise above 8.1 percent of gross domestic product. (KRUNGTHEP THURAKIJ)

- Customs tax on more than 1,600 import products is expected to be cut in the new year, a move likely to bring all import duties in Thailand below 30 percent. Some say the planned tariff reductions has dragged on too long because of claims, particularly by the petrochemical sector, that tariff reductions will harm some industries. (BANGKOK POST)

- General Motors says they will penetrate the lower to medium passenger car market segment in the Asian region by introducing an "Opel car for Asia", a modified version of the German design suited to the Asian region by 1999 and to be built in Rayong province. (BUSINESS DAY)
